signals.title: AUD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Advantage
signals.text: AUD leads the G10 board this week with a 1W average gain of +1.437% across 4 pairs, while USD is the primary laggard down -0.843% across 9 pairs, opening a massive 2.280% leader-to-laggard spread. Backing the move, RBA policy rate at 4.60% against Fed at 4.00% delivers an OIS carry advantage of 72bp favoring AUD via AONIA 4.60% over SOFR 3.88%. Spot trades at 0.7031, holding above its SMA20 at 0.6979 while facing technical headwind from the steep SMA200 at 0.7047 where the prevailing downtrend tests short-term reversal risk. Leveraged funds hold net long +44,978 contracts at the 54th percentile of their 52-week range, confirming upside participation without reaching positioning exhaustion. The bilateral outperformance reflects sustained policy divergence as RBA hiking posture contrasts with broad dollar softening. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD, supported by carry advantage and G10 relative strength. Catalyst: Fed meeting 28 Oct — hike priced. Risk: Daily rejection below the SMA20 at 0.6979 invalidates the near-term recovery structure.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Geopolitical Carry Tension
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.13, holding below its SMA200 at 158.51 while 160.00 remains the key level that has previously triggered Ministry of Finance intervention warnings. Carry structurally supports the pair via a 275bp Fed-BoJ rate spread with Fed at 4.00% and BoJ at 1.25%, backed by a +265bp OIS carry advantage favoring USD. However, options pricing reveals clear hedging stress, with 1M 25d risk reversals at -1.86 printing an extreme put skew alongside ATM IV running at 7.2% against HV30 of 5.6% for a +1.7% vol premium. Middle East tensions centered on Iranian statements regarding the Strait of Hormuz reinforce downside tail risk, leaving options desks aggressively paying for downside protection despite negative speculative sentiment showing JPY COT net short -37,820 contracts. Carry dominates directional drift while VIX remains contained at 16.7, but intervention asymmetry caps topside momentum. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY, carry support checked by heavy options downside demand. Catalyst: Japan Core CPI release at 23:30 UTC. Risk: Spot break above 158.51 accompanied by risk reversal normalization toward parity.

signals.title: NZD/USD — CPI Disinflation + Negative ESI Pressure
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5705 after dropping toward 0.5692 following third-quarter New Zealand CPI, which printed at 3.7% y/y against 3.8% consensus expectations and 4.1% prior. The data undershoot reinforces New Zealand's Economic Surprise Index at -16.0, marking the weakest macroeconomic momentum in the G10 with persistent misses across key releases. Spot remains above its SMA20 at 0.5632 but well below its SMA50 at 0.5769 and SMA200 at 0.5839, reflecting a counter-trend pullback inside a dominant technical downtrend. Structurally, Fed policy rate at 4.00% versus RBNZ at 2.75% maintains a 125bp nominal policy spread and a +125bp OIS carry advantage favoring USD. The softer inflation trajectory directly challenges market pricing for aggressive RBNZ tightening, leaving speculative shorts vulnerable to broader macro deceleration. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD, driven by disinflation and negative economic surprises. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 28 Oct — hike priced. Risk: Sustained daily close above the SMA50 at 0.5769 clears medium-term overhead supply.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Speculative Short + Elevated Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1238, sitting below its SMA20 at 1.1263, SMA50 at 1.1459, and SMA200 at 1.1586 in a broader structural downtrend. CFTC positioning shows leveraged funds holding net short -92,833 contracts, anchored at the 4th percentile of the 52-week range with a z-score of -1.78, indicating stretched institutional positioning. In the options market, 1M implied volatility trades at 6.6% against realized 30-day volatility of 4.1%, generating a notable +2.5% volatility risk premium that reflects substantial hedging demand. Meanwhile, Fed at 4.00% versus ECB at 2.65% maintains a 135bp carry advantage favoring USD, supported by a +144bp OIS spread via SOFR over €STR. The combination of stretched short positioning and high option premia leaves the pair prone to sharp short-covering bounces despite persistent carry headwinds. Trade bias: Range/neutral EUR/USD, downside limited by crowded positioning. Catalyst: ECB meeting 29 Oct — hold priced. Risk: Weekly net leveraged funds selling pushing below the 95k contract threshold.
